1999-05-21: The Office of Fair Trading rebuked Rupert Murdoch's Times for anti-competitive behavior over its cover price cuts and received an assurance from News International that it would not cut the Times's cover price without providing detailed explanation and financial information 10 days in advance.
1999-07-05: Rupert Murdoch said Peter Chernin would probably succeed him as chief executive of News Corporation, while indicating his children were not yet ready to take his place.
1999-12-01: Rupert Murdoch delivers a lecture in Oxford presenting a vision of technology empowering individuals and the internet as a force for change.
2000-05-16: News Corp president Peter Chernin said the company expects two or three other companies to take minority stakes in its soon-to-be-launched satellite internet concern, which is controlled by Rupert Murdoch.
2000-09-27: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation is in talks with Liberty Media to buy its $6bn holding in GemStar TV Guide, though the negotiations have yet to be finalised.
2000-10-06: Lachlan Murdoch, elder son of Rupert Murdoch, is appointed deputy chief operating officer at News Corporation, underlining his position as his father's eventual successor.
2001-02-07: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation reports a £200m first-half operating loss driven by failed internet investments, including the termination of two joint ventures with WebMD.
Rupert Murdoch is expected to confirm News Corporation's acquisition of DirecTV, paving the way for the flotation of Sky Global Networks.
2001-02-08: Rupert Murdoch is close to a deal to merge his satellite television operations with DirecTV, creating a $70bn business.
2001-02-27: Rupert Murdoch said merger talks between News Corporation and Hughes, the owner of DirecTV, were proceeding only slowly.
2001-02-28: Rupert Murdoch said due diligence was delaying a planned merger involving News Corporation’s Sky Global Networks and DirecTV parent Hughes Electronics.
2001-03-02: Rupert Murdoch has put on hold plans to float Sky Global Networks in New York due to volatile market conditions.
News Corp, led by Rupert Murdoch, denies reports that its takeover talks for DirecTV are on the verge of collapse, saying talks are ongoing and progressing slowly.
Rupert Murdoch's plans to take over Hughes Electronics, owner of DirecTV, are on the verge of collapse after negotiations with General Motors reached an impasse.
2001-04-23: Rupert Murdoch personally takes control of negotiations to rescue his takeover bid for Hughes Electronics Corp by meeting General Motors executives in Detroit.
2001-05-09: News Corp president Peter Chernin says there are no sticking points in Rupert Murdoch's News Corp takeover of DirecTV, as the deal nears its final stages.
2001-05-17: Rupert Murdoch’s News Corporation is in talks to acquire Hughes’ satellite business, with a potential rival bid emerging and Murdoch estimating the deal’s chances at 50-50.
2001-07-16: DirecTV, the satellite broadcaster sought by Rupert Murdoch, warned of sharply slowing subscriber numbers and cut its subscriber and revenue forecasts, as News Corporation was reported to be close to acquiring DirecTV after rival EchoStar reportedly abandoned its bid.
2001-08-16: Rupert Murdoch defended News Corporation’s bid for DirecTV, saying it offered a healthy premium for shareholders.
2001-09-12: Rupert Murdoch and John Malone will not be attending this week's Royal Television Society Cambridge Convention because of the tragedy in New York.
2001-09-21: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation says it is pressing ahead with its multibillion-pound takeover bid for DirecTV despite uncertainty following the attacks on America.
2001-10-28: Rupert Murdoch pulls News Corp out of its deal to take over Hughes Electronics, which includes DirecTV, saying he feels "deceived."
2001-11-02: Rupert Murdoch rules out BSkyB bidding for a terrestrial TV station or bailing out ITV Digital.
2001-11-08: The BBC and ITV are in preliminary talks to form a digital coalition to compete against Rupert Murdoch's BSkyB and other pay-television operators.
2001-11-15: Rupert Murdoch is in talks to sell BSkyB's 22% stake in KirchPayTV to John Malone's Liberty Media.
2001-11-18: Rupert Murdoch's third wife, Wendi Deng, gave birth to a daughter, Grace, making Murdoch a father for the fifth time at age 70.
2001-11-20: The government is considering lifting restrictions that bar Rupert Murdoch from owning an ITV licence.
The birth of Grace Murdoch, daughter of Rupert Murdoch, is noted as having no immediate effect on the succession question at News Corporation.
2002-01-25: Chase Carey, the third most senior executive at News Corporation and architect of Rupert Murdoch's global strategy, quits after 14 years following Murdoch's failure to acquire DirecTV.
2002-02-25: Rupert Murdoch promises News Corporation will increase its presence in Europe despite the collapse of its relationship with the Kirch Group, while ruling out further investment in Kirch as it currently exists.
2002-03-27: ITV Digital collapsed after a competitive battle with Rupert Murdoch's BSkyB, which had been excluded from the original digital terrestrial television consortium by regulators.
2002-06-11: Rupert Murdoch hints that after he retires, responsibility for running News Corporation will be shared more equally between his sons Lachlan and James than previously thought.
2002-06-12: The BBC plans a joint bid with BSkyB, controlled by Rupert Murdoch, for digital television licences freed by ITV Digital's demise, raising political questions over Murdoch's influence.
2002-06-13: The BBC unexpectedly joins forces with Rupert Murdoch's BSkyB to bid for the defunct ITV Digital licences, competing against a rival bid from Granada, Carlton, and Channel 4.
2002-06-15: The BBC and Crown Castle announce a joint bid with Rupert Murdoch's BSkyB to take over the defunct ITV Digital's airwaves for a free-to-air digital television service.
2002-06-20: Rupert Murdoch vows to stay at the helm of his media empire until he is 100 years old.
2002-07-31: BSkyB, controlled by Rupert Murdoch, reported a boost in subscribers and narrowed losses for the year, partly due to the collapse of rival ITV Digital.
2002-09-19: A television company controlled by Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation faces a second lawsuit in six months, as DirecTV sues NDS alleging fraud and misappropriation of trade secrets.
2002-09-25: Antitrust staff at the US Justice Department reportedly recommended blocking Echostar’s proposed $18bn buyout of DirecTV, potentially giving Rupert Murdoch’s News Corporation another opportunity to acquire DirecTV.
2002-10-10: Regulators blocked the merger of EchoStar and DirecTV, reopening the door for Rupert Murdoch to bid for a place in the US satellite broadcasting market.
2002-11-13: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation raised £820m through a share sale, fuelling speculation of another bid for DirecTV.
2002-11-24: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation reportedly held secret talks with DirecTV advisers about a potential $30 billion merger.
2002-12-10: Echostar Communications cancels its proposed £11.4bn takeover of Hughes Electronics, enabling Rupert Murdoch to revive his global satellite TV ambitions.
2002-12-18: Rupert Murdoch met representatives of General Motors, the controlling shareholder of DirecTV, in a renewed approach to acquire the US satellite broadcaster.
2003-02-04: Rupert Murdoch, aged 71, is expecting his sixth child with his third wife Wendi Deng, due in the summer.
2003-02-12: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation is expected to report its fourth successive quarter of growth as he prepares for a new battle for control of DirecTV.
2003-02-14: Rupert Murdoch appoints his son James as a non-executive director on the BSkyB board, boosting his family's presence on the board of the UK's largest pay TV broadcaster.
2003-02-26: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation appears to have decided to bid on its own for DirecTV owner Hughes Electronics, potentially pitting him against ally John Malone's Liberty Media, which is considering a separate bid.
2003-03-18: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation raised $1.35bn through a bond exchangeable into BSkyB shares to help fund a potential bid for DirecTV.
2003-03-28: Rupert Murdoch gives John Malone's Liberty Media an option to buy $500m of News Corporation stock, strengthening their position for a possible joint bid for DirecTV owner Hughes Electronics.
2003-03-29: Liberty Media backed away from challenging Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation in a bid for Hughes Corporation and instead decided to back Murdoch's bid, increasing its stake in News Corp from 17.5% to 19%.
2003-04-09: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation agrees a $6.6bn deal to take control of Hughes Electronics, parent company of DirecTV.
2003-04-10: Rupert Murdoch agreed a deal giving him control of satellite operator DirecTV for £4.1bn.
2003-04-13: Rupert Murdoch's News Corp agreed to acquire General Motors' 34 per cent stake in Hughes Electronics, owner of DirecTV, with a termination fee of up to $300m payable to News Corp if the deal fails to close under certain circumstances.
2003-08-13: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation returned to profit in the fourth quarter, reporting a £230m profit compared with a £1.08bn loss a year earlier.
2003-08-29: News Corporation sold its 8.1% stake in Japanese satellite TV company Sky PerfecTV! for £145m to Japanese shareholders Sony, Fuji Television, and Itochu.
2003-09-16: Rupert Murdoch faced a corporate governance row at BSkyB as City fund managers expressed dismay over his apparent move to install his son James as the satellite broadcaster's new chief executive.
2003-09-24: A leading pension fund group joins the row over BSkyB's future by demanding answers over Rupert Murdoch's plans to install his youngest son, James, as the company's new chief executive.
2003-09-29: DirecTV raised its revenue and subscriber targets for the full year, giving prospective owner Rupert Murdoch something to cheer about.
2003-10-07: The UK government cleared the £4.5bn merger of ITV broadcasters Carlton and Granada, creating a stronger competitor to Rupert Murdoch's pay TV group BSkyB.
2003-10-15: Rupert Murdoch said at News Corporation's annual general meeting that his retirement plans had been put on hold "forever" and that he would have to be "carried out."
2003-10-31: The National Association of Pension Funds backs Rupert Murdoch’s election of his son James Murdoch to the BSkyB board but calls for the ouster of Lord St John of Fawsley and recommends rejecting BSkyB’s remuneration policy.
2003-11-14: Rupert Murdoch faced a shareholder rebellion at BSkyB's annual general meeting over the appointment of his son James as chief executive, but the rebellion was crushed as key votes were won, though with significant dissent.
2003-12-03: US regulators are set to approve News Corp's takeover of DirecTV, likely with conditions to limit Rupert Murdoch's market influence.
2003-12-22: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation completed a £3.8bn deal to acquire DirecTV, giving it control of the largest US satellite pay-TV company.
2004-01-07: Rupert Murdoch hinted that he may share power between his sons Lachlan and James when he eventually hands over control of News Corp, while saying his succession remained an open question.
2004-01-22: John Malone becomes the second largest voting shareholder in Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation after increasing his stake to 9%, raising questions about Murdoch's succession plans.
2004-03-16: US media mogul John Malone declares himself a supporter of Rupert Murdoch and his family after building a 9% voting stake in News Corporation, hinting at possible future collaboration between Liberty Media and News Corp.
2004-05-06: Rupert Murdoch promised increased cooperation between his global pay-TV companies but ruled out reviving plans for a global satellite network, as News Corporation reported a 69% rise in quarterly net profits.
2004-07-13: A documentary titled "Outfoxed: Rupert Murdoch's War on Journalism" accuses Rupert Murdoch's Fox News of bias, prompting Fox News to react angrily to the bias allegations and unauthorized use of clips.
2004-10-11: Institutional Shareholder Services criticizes Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation for corporate governance failings, including its dual-class share structure, ahead of the company's relisting in New York.
2004-10-26: News Corporation shareholders approve Rupert Murdoch's plan to move the company's headquarters and primary stock market listing from Australia to the US.
2004-11-03: John Malone's Liberty Media announces a share swap with Merrill Lynch involving 84.7 million News Corp shares, a move that would nearly double Malone's voting stake in Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation to about 17%.
2004-11-04: Rupert Murdoch's New York Post received a subpoena from the US attorney's office in Brooklyn as part of an investigation into newspaper circulation practices.
2004-11-12: Rupert Murdoch called an emergency board meeting and announced a "poison pill" takeover defence after John Malone moved to almost double his stake in News Corporation to 17%.
BSkyB shareholders approve a buyback plan that will increase Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation stake in the pay-television firm by 2 percentage points to 37%.
2004-12-05: John Malone doubles his stake in News Corp to 17 percent, prompting Rupert Murdoch to unveil a "poison pill" defence to prevent further increases.
2004-12-07: Liberty Media CEO Robert Bennett said the two sides were talking, indicating a possible détente between Rupert Murdoch and John Malone.
2004-12-17: Rupert Murdoch reportedly bid $44 million for a Fifth Avenue penthouse in Manhattan, which if accepted would be the most expensive apartment purchase in Manhattan, though the contract has not yet been signed.
2004-12-21: John Malone accelerated a plan to double his voting shares in News Corporation, a move seen as a potential threat to Rupert Murdoch's succession plan.
2005-02-02: News Corporation, controlled by Rupert Murdoch, reported a 25% decline in operating income at News International for the last three months of 2004, attributed to costs from new printing presses.
2005-02-16: Rupert Murdoch led a meeting of more than 50 senior News Corporation executives in New York to map out the group's internet strategy.
2005-04-13: Rupert Murdoch warned newspaper editors that the industry had been complacent about the internet and must adapt to digital challenges.
2005-04-15: Rupert Murdoch admits in a speech to American editors in Washington that he and the media industry were complacent about digital media and the internet.
2005-07-18: News Corp, chaired by Rupert Murdoch, announces it will acquire Intermix Media for $580 million, including the social networking site MySpace.
2005-07-22: Pace Micro Technology signs a deal to supply set-top boxes to Rupert Murdoch's US satellite television operation DirecTV.
2005-07-29: Lachlan Murdoch stood down from his job at News Corp, leaving James Murdoch in pole position to succeed Rupert Murdoch.
2005-08-07: News Corp shareholders object to restrictions Rupert Murdoch wanted to impose on share dealing, while the European Commission threatens his BSkyB football broadcast near-monopoly and the Barclay brothers escalate their campaign against him.
2005-08-10: Rupert Murdoch outlined plans for News Corporation to invest an additional $1bn in online properties and disclosed that the company is in advanced negotiations to acquire a controlling stake in a search engine.
2005-08-15: Rupert Murdoch appointed Roger Ailes as head of the Fox Television Stations group, replacing his son Lachlan.
2005-08-16: News Corporation announces that Roger Ailes will take charge of Fox Television Studios, a responsibility previously held by Lachlan Murdoch.
2005-08-19: Rupert Murdoch appoints John Hartigan to replace his son Lachlan as chairman of News Corporation's Australian operations, effective September 1.
2005-09-08: News Corporation, led by Rupert Murdoch, acquired online video gaming company IGN Entertainment for £353.4m.
2005-10-03: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation announces the sale of its education titles, including the Times Educational Supplement, for £235m.
2005-10-21: Rupert Murdoch faces a threatened rebellion by News Corp shareholders over the extension of a "poison pill" plan to stop John Malone building his stake in News Corp, and expects a rough ride from investors at the BSkyB AGM over a buyback plan that would increase News Corp's stake.
2005-11-04: Rupert Murdoch launched a record label and a music channel intended to compete with MTV.
2005-11-07: Rupert Murdoch promised that his successor at News Corporation will be chosen by the company's independent directors, while defending his son James's record and not discounting keeping the position in the family.
2005-11-24: Rupert Murdoch gave his first British interview in five years, defending his legacy and complaining about resentment from the BBC and establishment forces.
2006-01-04: News Corporation chairman Rupert Murdoch promoted Jeremy Philips to executive vice-president in the office of the chairman, overseeing the company's internet investments.
2006-03-13: Rupert Murdoch delivered a speech in London predicting that the internet would dominate media access, that newspapers might become news-sites, and that power would shift away from the old media elite.
2006-06-20: MySpace, owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation, plans to expand into Europe using Britain as a beachhead, with 11 countries earmarked including France and Germany.
2006-07-17: News Corporation boss Rupert Murdoch, having embarked on a $2bn spending spree on new media properties including MySpace, warns that old media barons who do not embrace the digital revolution will fail.
2006-09-17: Rupert Murdoch is considering selling his 38% stake in DirecTV to rival John Malone in exchange for Malone’s 19% stake in News Corporation, in a move aimed at protecting Murdoch’s control of News Corp.
2006-10-04: Rupert Murdoch says his eldest son Lachlan might return to a senior position at News Corporation, more than a year after Lachlan quit as chief operating officer.
2006-10-06: Brad Greenspan, co-founder of MySpace's former owner Intermix Media, calls for a federal investigation into Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation purchase of MySpace, alleging executives conspired to sell the site for a criminally low price.
2006-10-12: Liberty Media publicly confirms it is in discussions with News Corp chairman Rupert Murdoch over swapping its roughly $11bn stake in News Corp for a controlling stake in DirecTV.
2006-10-20: Rupert Murdoch won shareholder approval to extend News Corp's "poison pill" scheme, designed to prevent John Malone from increasing his stake, until October 2008.
2006-11-17: BSkyB, 39% owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation, acquired an 18% stake in ITV worth nearly £1bn without prior knowledge of ITV's board.
2006-11-27: NTL prepares submissions to Ofcom and the Office of Fair Trading contesting BSkyB's acquisition of a 17.9% stake in ITV, a move by the company 39% owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation.
2006-12-03: James Murdoch revealed that BSkyB's £940m purchase of a 17.9% stake in ITV was his idea, not his father Rupert Murdoch's.
2006-12-07: Rupert Murdoch is reportedly on the brink of signing a deal with rival John Malone that would allow him to retain control of News Corporation.
2006-12-22: Rupert Murdoch finalised a deal with John Malone under which News Corp will buy back Malone's 16.3% stake, strengthening Murdoch's control of News Corporation.
2007-01-21: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation acquired two newspaper groups with 28 weekly papers primarily serving Queens and Brooklyn.
2007-01-26: News of the World royal editor Clive Goodman pleaded guilty to illegal phone hacking, a practice later alleged in a letter to have been carried out with the full knowledge and support of News International editorial executives under Rupert Murdoch's ownership.
2007-02-26: The UK government launched an inquiry into whether Rupert Murdoch's BSkyB purchase of a 17.9% stake in ITV raises public interest concerns about media ownership.
2007-04-04: News Corp shareholders overwhelmingly approved an $11bn asset swap that increases Rupert Murdoch's control over the company, lifting the Murdoch family's stake to 38% from 31%.
2007-04-27: The Office of Fair Trading and Ofcom warn that BSkyB's acquisition of a 17.9% stake in ITV raises significant competition concerns, setting the government on a collision course with Rupert Murdoch.
2007-05-02: The Dow Jones board decided to take no action on Rupert Murdoch's $5bn takeover bid, citing opposition from the Bancroft family, which controls 64% of the voting stock.
2007-05-03: The Times editor Robert Thomson is to fly to California to discuss News Corporation's bid for Dow Jones with Rupert Murdoch, who is hosting a gathering of senior management near his Carmel ranch.
2007-05-08: Rupert Murdoch accused the government of "chickening out" of ruling on BSkyB's acquisition of a 17.9% stake in ITV and defended the move as legal.
2007-05-09: Rupert Murdoch defends BSkyB's acquisition of a 17.9% stake in ITV and says he is unworried by the threat of a competition inquiry.
2007-05-11: Rupert Murdoch sent a letter to the Bancroft family pledging not to interfere with the Wall Street Journal's editorial independence and offering them a seat on the News Corp board as part of his $5bn bid for Dow Jones.
2007-05-20: Rupert Murdoch met with Sunday Telegraph editor Patience Wheatcroft, Times editor Robert Thomson, and Times business editor James Harding in New York, amid reports that Thomson is being lined up to edit the Wall Street Journal if Murdoch succeeds in his bid to acquire Dow Jones.
2007-05-24: UK Trade Secretary Alistair Darling referred BSkyB's acquisition of a 17.9% stake in ITV to the Competition Commission, opening a full investigation into Rupert Murdoch's media influence.
2007-06-01: The Bancroft family, which controls Dow Jones, agreed to enter talks with Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation over his $5bn bid for the company, ending a month of resistance.
2007-06-04: Rupert Murdoch met with the Bancroft family, the controlling shareholders of Dow Jones, in a four-hour meeting that was seen as a positive step toward his $5bn takeover bid.
2007-06-26: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation is reported to have agreed terms to protect the editorial independence of the Wall Street Journal, potentially paving the way for his $5bn takeover of Dow Jones.
2007-07-06: Takeover talks between Dow Jones and Rupert Murdoch’s News Corp are progressing, but no deal has been completed.
Rupert Murdoch reportedly succeeded with his $5bn bid for Dow Jones, with News Corporation completing negotiations with the Dow Jones board, though a formal announcement is expected next week.
2007-07-09: The Competition Commission confirms its inquiry into BSkyB's 17.9% stake in ITV will include an investigation of the link between the satellite broadcaster and the rest of Rupert Murdoch's media empire.
2007-07-16: Rupert Murdoch is preparing for a meeting with Dow Jones this week over his $5bn takeover plan, while Bancroft family member Christopher Bancroft reportedly works to block the sale.
2007-07-17: The Dow Jones board voted to accept Rupert Murdoch's $5bn takeover bid, leaving the controlling Bancroft family to consider whether to back the deal.
2007-07-23: The Bancroft family’s opposition to Rupert Murdoch’s $5bn takeover bid for Dow Jones reportedly hardened at a family meeting, with one member invoking journalist Daniel Pearl, making the outcome increasingly in doubt.
2007-07-30: The Bancroft family remains split over whether to sell Dow Jones and the Wall Street Journal to Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation, as Murdoch's deadline to finalize the deal looms.
2007-07-31: News Corporation, led by Rupert Murdoch, is reportedly edging closer to a deal to buy Dow Jones, with an announcement expected today, as Bancroft family support for the $5bn takeover increases.
2007-08-01: Rupert Murdoch clinched ownership of Dow Jones, publisher of the Wall Street Journal, after key members of the controlling Bancroft family switched sides to back his $5bn takeover bid.
2007-09-14: Peter Chernin, president and chief operating officer of Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation, told British broadcasters at the Royal Television Society convention that they must innovate or face extinction.
2007-09-18: Rupert Murdoch said he aims to make $100m in savings at Dow Jones following News Corporation's acquisition of the company.
2007-10-08: Rupert Murdoch, whose News Corporation's acquisition of Dow Jones is not expected to complete until December, has been visiting the Wall Street Journal's New York headquarters to meet executives and staff and critique the paper's coverage.
2007-10-17: Rupert Murdoch outlined plans to move the Wall Street Journal beyond its financial roots and target mainstream competitors such as the New York Times, ahead of completing his $5bn takeover of Dow Jones.
2007-10-25: Rupert Murdoch's acquisition of Dow Jones, and therefore the Wall Street Journal, is described as the media story of the year, though he has yet to clear regulatory hurdles before assuming complete control.
2007-11-01: The Australian newspaper introduces content from the Wall Street Journal, in a deal likely to be the first in a series tying the financial title more closely with Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation media empire.
2007-11-02: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation-owned newspaper The Australian begins carrying a daily branded Wall Street Journal page in its business section under a partnership deal.
2007-12-07: Rupert Murdoch confirms the appointment of his son James Murdoch as chairman and chief executive of News Corporation in Europe and Asia, and Les Hinton as chief executive of Dow Jones.
2007-12-13: News Corporation, led by Rupert Murdoch, is due to officially complete its $5bn acquisition of Dow Jones, owner of the Wall Street Journal, with a shareholder vote formalizing the deal.
2007-12-14: Rupert Murdoch celebrates News Corporation's acquisition of the Wall Street Journal with a $2m global advertising campaign.
2007-12-15: Dow Jones shareholders formally approve Rupert Murdoch's bid to acquire the company.
2008-01-21: Lachlan Murdoch is expected to take a 50% stake in a joint venture with James Packer to privatise Consolidated Media Holdings, becoming executive chairman.
2008-02-11: News Corp, led by Rupert Murdoch, is reported to be in discussions to merge MySpace and other News Corp internet properties with Yahoo in return for a 20% stake in the combined company.
2008-02-13: News Corp, led by Rupert Murdoch, is reportedly considering a plan to take around a 20% stake in Yahoo in exchange for MySpace and other digital assets, as Yahoo seeks alternatives to Microsoft's hostile takeover bid.
2008-04-07: Lachlan Murdoch's A$3.2bn bid for control of Consolidated Media Holdings, backed by Rupert Murdoch, collapsed over price.
2008-05-30: Rupert Murdoch praised Barack Obama as a "rock star" and said he had played a part in the New York Post's endorsement of Obama, while stopping short of a full personal endorsement.
2008-07-13: Rupert Murdoch falls to his lowest ranking in the MediaGuardian 100, attributed to his completed $5.6bn takeover of Wall Street Journal parent company Dow Jones and his focus on the US financial paper.
2008-07-16: News Corp, owned by Rupert Murdoch, is said to be having preliminary discussions with Mort Zuckerman about joint printing and distribution arrangements for the New York Post and Daily News.
2008-10-16: Rupert Murdoch criticized British regulators for ordering BSkyB to reduce its 17.9% stake in ITV to less than 7.5%, calling it a "huge injustice."
2008-10-17: Rupert Murdoch criticized British regulators for ordering BSkyB to reduce its 17.9% stake in ITV to less than 7.5%, calling it a "huge injustice."
2008-11-21: Roger Ailes, founder of Fox News and key lieutenant of Rupert Murdoch, signed a new five-year agreement to remain chairman and CEO of Fox News and chairman of Fox Television Stations, and senior adviser to Murdoch.
2009-03-02: News Corporation chairman and chief executive Rupert Murdoch is planning to relinquish substantial powers to son James and for him to take a major role in the US, leaving Sun editor Rebekah Wade to assume greater control of the media group's UK operation.
2009-06-03: Rupert Murdoch appoints Chase Carey as deputy chairman, president, and chief operating officer of News Corp, replacing Peter Chernin as his second in command.
2009-06-23: Rupert Murdoch is openly discussing the possibility of charging for online access to the Times or the Sun.
2009-08-05: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation reported a $3.4bn net loss for the 12 months to June, its worst year in recent memory.
2009-09-07: News Corp, approved by chairman and CEO Rupert Murdoch, is launching NewsCore, a global service to make all its news stories and videos instantly available across its TV, print, and online outlets, though a launch date has not been set.
2009-11-11: A former senior editor, Sandra Guzman, files a discrimination lawsuit against Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation, the New York Post, and editor-in-chief Col Allan, alleging racist and sexist behavior and claiming her September dismissal was retaliatory.
2009-12-01: Rupert Murdoch reiterated his belief that internet users will pay for news content and criticized news aggregation as "theft" in an address to US media regulators.
2010-01-21: The court of appeal ruled that BSkyB, in which Rupert Murdoch's News Corp is the largest shareholder, must more than halve its 17.9% stake in ITV and denied permission for a further appeal.
2010-06-16: News Corp, controlled by Rupert Murdoch, plans to take full control of BSkyB by bidding for the 61% it does not already own.
2010-09-09: During a parliamentary debate, Labour MP Tom Watson accused Rupert Murdoch of appointing Rebekah Brooks as chief executive of News International despite knowing she had admitted illegal payments were made to police by the News of the World, and recommended Murdoch be summoned to give evidence to the Commons standards and privileges committee.
2010-10-15: Rupert Murdoch told News Corporation's annual general meeting that there were very strict rules and that a person who bought a bugged conversation more than five years earlier was immediately fired, while saying the company would take immediate action if anything came to light.
2010-11-30: News Corp COO Chase Carey said the company is open to all options for Rupert Murdoch's MySpace, including a possible sale.
2011-01-24: Rupert Murdoch arrived in London and abandoned plans to attend the World Economic Forum in Davos amid the News of the World phone-hacking scandal.
2011-02-02: Rupert Murdoch dodged questions about the widening phone-hacking scandal at the press launch of the Daily and missed News Corp's quarterly reports Q&A session.
2011-02-27: Lord Prescott claims in the House of Lords that the phone-hacking investigation has been extended to the Sunday Times, another title in Rupert Murdoch's media empire, while News International denies that any of its titles other than the News of the World are under investigation.
2011-03-16: A YouGov poll commissioned by Avaaz found that almost 60% of British people believe Rupert Murdoch has too much political influence and 64% believe a full News Corporation takeover of BSkyB would give him too much power over the media.
2011-04-07: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation admitted liability and issued an unreserved apology in eight phone-hacking lawsuits against the News of the World, aiming to settle cases and contain the scandal.
2011-04-08: Rupert Murdoch's News International issued a public apology to eight phone-hacking victims and admitted for the first time that voicemail interception was rife at the News of the World, offering compensation to some of the 24 high-profile figures suing the paper.
2011-04-10: James Weatherup, a veteran reporter at Rupert Murdoch's News of the World, was arrested in connection with the phone-hacking scandal, complicating News Corp's efforts to contain the affair.
2011-04-15: News Corporation, owned by Rupert Murdoch, made a £100,000 offer of damages to Sienna Miller to settle her phone-hacking case, as disclosed in the high court by its lawyers.
2011-05-03: Media Matters for America publishes a full-page ad in the International Herald Tribune criticizing News Corporation and calling on James Murdoch to reform the company, invoking Rupert Murdoch as the representative of the old News Corp.
2011-06-30: Rupert Murdoch’s News Corporation received regulatory approval to take over BSkyB, subject to conditions including spinning off Sky News, though the deal was expected to cost nearly £2bn more than originally planned.
2011-07-06: The phone-hacking crisis at the News of the World, owned by Rupert Murdoch's News International, intensified as it emerged that relatives of 7/7 bombing victims were targeted, and Graham Foulkes said he would like to meet Murdoch to discuss the allegations.
2011-07-07: Pressure mounts on Rupert Murdoch to contain the phone hacking scandal within the UK before it spills over into his US media interests, following the closure of the News of the World.
Rupert Murdoch closes down the News of the World for good amid phone hacking revelations.
2011-07-08: Rebekah Brooks discussed with James Murdoch an internal investigation into phone hacking that might "slam Les, Colin etc" and "vindicate" her position, potentially saving her job but damaging Rupert Murdoch's right-hand man Les Hinton.
2011-07-09: Trinity Mirror newspapers, including the Daily Mirror, launch a campaign of vilification against Rupert Murdoch and News International over the phone hacking scandal, with front-page headlines such as "Toxic" and "The Wapping Cowboy."
2011-07-10: Rupert Murdoch asked Rebekah Brooks not to resign on the day the News of the World closed.
2011-07-11: The government referred Rupert Murdoch's £8bn bid to take full control of BSkyB to the Competition Commission after News Corp withdrew an offer to spin off Sky News.
2011-07-12: Rupert Murdoch, James Murdoch, and Rebekah Brooks are invited to appear before the Commons culture select committee over the phone-hacking scandal, with News International stating it will cooperate and await the formal invitation.
2011-07-14: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation calls in PR firm Edelman to help handle mounting public anger and political pressure over the UK phone-hacking scandal.
Rupert Murdoch and his son James agree to give evidence to a Commons committee investigating phone hacking after parliament threatens them with imprisonment.
2011-07-15: Rebekah Brooks resigned as chief executive of News International, the UK arm of Rupert Murdoch's empire, amid the phone-hacking scandal.
Rupert Murdoch made a "full and humble" apology to the family of murdered schoolgirl Milly Dowler at a private meeting in London, repeatedly saying he was "very, very sorry."
2011-07-17: A lawyer leading the phone-hacking legal challenge says that without "no win, no fee" agreements, Rupert Murdoch's News of the World would still be published, and warns that government proposals to curb such agreements threaten access to justice for hacking victims.
2011-07-19: Rupert Murdoch expressed regret for News Corporation's involvement in the phone-hacking scandal while insisting he was kept in the dark, during a parliamentary committee hearing.

Rupert Murdoch and his son James Murdoch give evidence to a Commons select committee about the phone-hacking scandal, with Rupert Murdoch saying he must be careful not to prejudice the course of justice.

Former News of the World editor Colin Myler and former News International legal manager Tom Crone said James Murdoch had been "mistaken" when he told a House of Commons select committee that he had not been aware in 2008 of the "For Neville" email.
2011-07-20: A parliamentary committee found that Rupert Murdoch's News International "deliberately" tried to block a Scotland Yard criminal investigation into phone hacking at the News of the World.

Evidence obtained by the Guardian indicates that James Murdoch gave misleading parliamentary testimony about a phone-hacking cover-up, contradicting his denial that astronomical sums were secretly paid as hush money to hacking victim Gordon Taylor, with Rupert Murdoch accompanying his son at the committee hearing.
2011-07-21: Rupert Murdoch and his son James pleaded ignorance of the full extent of alleged illegal practices at News International during an appearance before the culture, media and sport select committee.
2011-08-10: A New York Times article reports that several of News Corporation's independent directors have deep personal and business ties to Rupert Murdoch, raising corporate governance concerns.
2011-09-13: Rupert Murdoch's UK subsidiary told the high court it had found "tens of thousands" of extra emails potentially shedding light on the extent of phone hacking at the News of the World.
2011-09-20: News International, parent group of the News of the World, confirms it is in advanced negotiations with the family of Milly Dowler for a settlement involving a £1m donation from Rupert Murdoch to a charity of the family's choice and a separate £2m payout, though no final agreement has yet been reached.

Ted Turner says Rupert Murdoch will have to step down in the wake of the phone-hacking controversy, though Murdoch has consistently denied knowledge of the alleged extent of phone hacking at the News of the World.
2011-10-03: UK cabinet minister Michael Gove praises Rupert Murdoch as "a great man" at his party's annual conference.
2011-10-10: Institutional Shareholder Services advises shareholders to vote 13 of News Corporation's 15 directors, including Rupert Murdoch and his sons James and Lachlan, off the board ahead of the 21 October shareholder meeting.
2011-10-21: News Corp shareholders voted against the re-election of Rupert Murdoch and his sons to the board and rejected his $33m pay package at the company's annual meeting in Los Angeles.
Hermes Equity Ownership Services advises clients to withhold support from five News Corp directors, including Rupert Murdoch, at the company's annual meeting.
2011-11-03: News Corp announced that closing the News of the World cost Rupert Murdoch's company $91m.
2011-11-05: Rebekah Brooks, a favourite of Rupert Murdoch, received a £1.7m pay-off, the use of a London office and a chauffeur-driven limousine as part of her severance package from News International after resigning amid the phone-hacking scandal.
2011-12-09: The government disclosed that Rupert Murdoch attended a previously undisclosed second meeting with David Cameron at Downing Street in July 2010, shortly after News Corporation launched its bid to take over BSkyB.
2011-12-12: Tessa Jowell accepts a £200,000 settlement from Rupert Murdoch's News International over the hacking of her phone.
2011-12-22: The Council of Institutional Investors called on News Corp directors to end the dual-class stock structure that reinforces Rupert Murdoch's dominance over the company.
2012-01-09: Elisabeth Murdoch is announced to deliver the 2012 MacTaggart lecture, following her father Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation buyout of her company Shine.
2012-01-19: Lawyers for phone-hacking victims accuse directors of Rupert Murdoch's News Group Newspapers of concealing wrongdoing by deliberately deceiving investigators and destroying evidence.
2012-02-08: News International, Rupert Murdoch's UK newspaper publisher, faces more than 50 new damages claims from alleged victims of News of the World phone hacking, after already settling more than 50 civil actions.
2012-02-14: News Corporation, led by Rupert Murdoch, reported $200m in costs from the News of the World phone hacking scandal, including $87m in the final quarter of 2011 and $108m in the previous quarter.
2012-03-13: Rupert Murdoch was among those at the Long Island funeral for war correspondent Marie Colvin, who was killed trying to escape Homs shelling.
2012-04-03: Shareholder activists renewed their call for Rupert Murdoch to quit as chairman of News Corporation amid the phone-hacking scandal and James Murdoch's resignation as BSkyB chairman.
2012-04-25: Rupert Murdoch admitted in written evidence to the Leveson inquiry that he was disappointed the Times published the Nightjack story and that he had not bought the MPs' expenses files.
Rupert Murdoch is due to give evidence to the Leveson inquiry into phone hacking and media ethics, with a day and a half set aside for his appearance.
2012-04-26: Ofcom examines phone-hacking evidence as part of its investigation into whether Rupert Murdoch's News Corp is a "fit and proper" owner of a BSkyB broadcasting licence.

Rupert Murdoch apologises at the Leveson inquiry for his shortcomings in the News of the World phone-hacking scandal, admitting there was a "cover-up" at the tabloid and that he had been "misinformed and shielded".
Former News of the World legal manager Tom Crone accused Rupert Murdoch of telling a "shameful lie" at the Leveson inquiry by alleging Crone took charge of a cover-up of phone hacking.
2012-05-01: A Washington-based ethics watchdog calls on federal regulators to revoke News Corporation's 27 Fox broadcast licences following a UK parliamentary report that concluded Rupert Murdoch was not fit to run a major international company.

A UK parliamentary select committee report concluded that Rupert Murdoch is "not a fit person" to run a major international company, a finding News Corporation called "unjustified and highly partisan."
A parliamentary committee report on phone hacking stopped short of declaring Rupert Murdoch unfit to run an international company after Conservative MPs refused to support that conclusion.
2012-05-02: US Senate commerce committee chairman Jay Rockefeller contacts Lord Justice Leveson to seek evidence on whether News Corp, led by Rupert Murdoch, broke US laws in the phone-hacking scandal.
2012-05-08: Prince Alwaleed bin Talal, a major News Corp shareholder, publicly expresses frustration that the phone-hacking scandal is harming the company's reputation while reaffirming his unwavering backing of Rupert Murdoch.
2012-05-18: Rupert Murdoch's London operation, NI Group, disclosed it spent £53.2m on its management and standards committee, bringing total costs from the phone-hacking scandal and News of the World closure to over £300m.
2012-06-20: Rupert Murdoch's News Limited made a A$2bn bid to acquire Consolidated Media Holdings, aiming to double its stake in Foxtel to 50% and Fox Sports to 100%, pending regulatory approval.
2012-06-21: News Corporation shareholders filed a lawsuit accusing the company's board of lax oversight, alleging directors turned a blind eye to phone hacking at News of the World for fear of angering Rupert Murdoch and his son James, and that Murdoch misused company resources for political gain.
2012-06-22: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation accepted 64 further claims into its compensation scheme for News of the World phone-hacking victims, as more than 70 claimants pursue civil action against News International.
2012-06-26: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation confirms it is considering a split into two separately listed public companies, separating its publishing assets from its film and TV businesses.
2012-06-28: News Corp's board approves a split of the company's entertainment and publishing assets, a move seen as a response to the UK phone-hacking scandal and a rearguard action by Rupert Murdoch.
Rupert Murdoch is expected to announce plans to split News Corp into separate entertainment and publishing companies.
2012-07-24: Eight people, including Andy Coulson and Rebekah Brooks, both former editors of Rupert Murdoch's News of the World, are charged with conspiring to hack the phones of more than 600 people.
2012-09-05: News Corporation cut the bonuses of four top executives, including Rupert Murdoch, due to the phone-hacking scandal, though Murdoch still received over $30m for the year to the end of June.
2012-09-11: Rupert Murdoch promotes News International chief information officer Paul Cheesbrough to News Corp chief technical officer, reporting directly to Murdoch.
2012-09-16: Rupert Murdoch has agreed to step down as chief executive of News Corporation's publishing business while remaining chairman, following the phone-hacking scandal.
2012-09-19: News Corp shareholders ask a US court for permission to sue Rupert Murdoch and the company's board for failing to stop the phone hacking scandal.
2012-09-20: News Corp shareholders reacted angrily to reports that James Murdoch could soon be given control of Fox Networks, News Corp's US TV business, with one dissident shareholder calling it a "slap in the face for shareholders."
2012-10-03: Shareholders, including Hermes and Glass Lewis, campaign to remove Rupert Murdoch as chairman of News Corporation ahead of the company's annual meeting.
2012-10-16: Rupert Murdoch faced down dissident shareholders at News Corp's annual meeting, defeating proposals for an independent chairman and an end to the dual-class share structure, though a majority of independent shareholders voted for separating the chief executive and chairman roles.
2012-10-21: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation is reportedly in early talks to acquire the Los Angeles Times and Chicago Tribune from the Tribune Company.
2012-11-29: The Leveson report criticised Rupert Murdoch for failing to react to evidence of "casual and cavalier" journalism at the News of the World, while recognising his business acumen and immense implicit power.
2012-12-03: Rupert Murdoch confirms that his new standalone publishing group will retain the News Corporation name, with the film and TV businesses to form a separate company named Fox Group.
2013-02-01: Rupert Murdoch's News International agrees out-of-court settlements on 143 of 165 outstanding civil phone-hacking damages cases ahead of a high court hearing.
2013-03-05: Rupert Murdoch's chief of staff, Natalie Ravitz, launched a Tumblr blog titled "Murdoch here" that recasts Murdoch as a fun-loving, globetrotting man of action.
2013-03-15: Detectives are examining an estimated 600 fresh allegations of phone-hacking incidents at Rupert Murdoch's now-closed News of the World after obtaining new evidence from a suspect turned supergrass.
2013-04-17: Rupert Murdoch announces that the entertainment division of News Corporation will be named 21st Century Fox when the company splits into two.
2013-04-22: News Corporation agrees to a $139m settlement of a shareholders' lawsuit alleging the board, including chairman Rupert Murdoch, ignored phone hacking at the News of the World, with the settlement to be funded by insurance covering the board.
2013-05-07: Dissident shareholders from the US, UK and Canada filed a resolution calling for News Corporation to appoint an independent chairman, pressing Rupert Murdoch to step down as chairman.
2013-05-29: Rupert Murdoch told investors at a New York meeting that he has been given the chance to do it all over again ahead of the 28 June split of News Corp into two separate companies.
2013-06-11: News Corp shareholders formally approve a plan to split the media giant's publishing assets from its entertainment division, with Rupert Murdoch to chair both companies.
2013-06-18: Rupert Murdoch splits his News Corporation empire into two companies, with entertainment assets forming 21st Century Fox and publishing assets trading under the old News Corp name.
2013-07-01: Rupert Murdoch's media empire officially split into two separately listed companies, with the newspaper and book publishing arms and Australian pay-TV assets retaining the News Corp name, while the Fox film and TV businesses and European and Asian pay-TV operations became 21st Century Fox.
2013-07-04: A leaked recording reveals Rupert Murdoch's private apology over the phone-hacking scandal was not genuine, as he belittled charges against staff, claimed to have withdrawn police cooperation, and promised to hit back.
2013-07-18: Rupert Murdoch admitted he was wrong to describe police investigations into his company and its journalists as "incompetent," while questioning the proportionality of the investigations.
2013-11-18: MySpace co-founder Chris DeWolfe accuses Rupert Murdoch of ruining the social network after News Corp bought it in 2005.
2014-03-11: Rupert Murdoch is to be inducted into the US television academy hall of fame.
2014-03-26: Rupert Murdoch appoints his eldest son Lachlan as co-chairman of News Corporation and 21st Century Fox, positioning him as the most likely successor.
2014-05-12: Rupert Murdoch revived a plan for BSkyB to buy out Sky Deutschland and Sky Italia, with BSkyB confirming preliminary discussions but no agreement reached.
2014-06-25: Scotland Yard wants to interview Rupert Murdoch about crime at his UK papers, having contacted the media mogul the previous year but agreeing with lawyers to wait until the end of the phone-hacking trial.
2014-07-19: Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox is pushing for an attempted $80bn acquisition of Time Warner.
2014-07-24: BSkyB is set to confirm a £10bn deal to create Sky Europe by buying sister pay-TV companies in Germany and Italy from Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox.
2014-11-18: News Corp shareholders narrowly defeated a proposal to scrap the dual-class share structure that gives the Murdoch family 39.4% voting control, with Rupert Murdoch opening the annual general meeting and endorsing his eldest son Lachlan as co-chairman.
2015-03-04: Rupert Murdoch's former UK publisher News International quietly settled a legal claim over email hacking brought by Jane Winter and British-Irish Rights Watch, without admitting liability.
2015-06-11: Rupert Murdoch is preparing to step down as chief executive of 21st Century Fox, handing the role to his youngest son James, in a reorganization expected to be ratified at a board meeting as early as next week.
2015-06-12: Rupert Murdoch is preparing to step down as chief executive of 21st Century Fox, with his sons James and Lachlan taking leading roles, while he continues as executive chairman.
2015-06-14: Rupert Murdoch is not stepping down at 21st Century Fox, while son James steps up as CEO and son Lachlan joins as executive co-chairman in a partnership arrangement.
2015-06-16: Rupert Murdoch confirmed he will stand down as chief executive of 21st Century Fox at the end of the month, handing over control to his son James, with the management changes approved by the company's board.
2015-09-02: Rupert Murdoch gives Rebekah Brooks back her old job as chief executive of his British newspapers, a decision described by insiders as bold and attributed to his disregard for what others think.
2015-12-11: UK prosecutors announce insufficient evidence to bring corporate charges against News UK over phone hacking, effectively clearing Rupert Murdoch's company.
2015-12-21: Rupert Murdoch attended a Christmas party that drew David Cameron, George Osborne, and other ministers, marking his return to the centre of British power.
2016-06-30: Rupert Murdoch's News Corp struck a £220m deal to buy Wireless Group, the owner of TalkSport.
2016-09-13: A new book by former News Corp Australia editor-in-chief Chris Mitchell reveals that Rupert Murdoch was devastated by the closeness between his then-wife Wendi Deng and Tony Blair.
2016-12-09: Sky's independent directors agree to an offer price of £10.75 per share in cash from 21st Century Fox, a company associated with Rupert Murdoch.
2016-12-12: Labour tables an urgent question in parliament about Rupert Murdoch's bid to take full control of Sky, with the government facing 10 working days to decide whether to issue a public interest intervention notice.

Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox has until 6 January to notify the UK takeover panel of its intention to proceed with its £11.2bn purchase of Sky, after which culture secretary Karen Bradley must decide whether to launch a public interest test.

Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox is planning to use a "scheme of arrangement" for its £11.2bn takeover of Sky, requiring 75% approval from non-Fox shareholders to force out opponents, while facing investor calls to raise the offer price.
2016-12-13: Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox is not expected to offer Sky News as a regulatory concession in its £11.2bn takeover bid for Sky, despite having done so during a previous acquisition attempt in 2011.
2016-12-14: Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox is expected to table a formal offer for Sky as soon as Thursday.
2016-12-15: Rupert Murdoch’s 21st Century Fox formally lodged an £11.7bn bid to take full control of Sky.
2017-02-05: An analysis by the Media Reform Coalition and 38 Degrees found that Rupert Murdoch-owned company executives met the prime minister or chancellor 10 times in the year to September 2016, more than any other media organisation, with 20 meetings over 18 months including seven involving Murdoch himself.
2017-03-01: Campaigners at the Media Reform Coalition and Avaaz submitted research urging the culture secretary to reject Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox bid for full control of Sky on competition grounds.
2017-03-03: UK culture secretary Karen Bradley said she is "minded to" refer Rupert Murdoch's £11.7bn takeover bid for Sky to Ofcom over media plurality and broadcasting standards concerns, but has not made a final decision.
2017-03-16: UK Culture Secretary Karen Bradley referred 21st Century Fox's £11.7bn bid for Sky to Ofcom to investigate public interest concerns over media plurality and broadcasting standards.
2017-03-31: Former Labour leader Ed Miliband and ex-business secretary Vince Cable submitted arguments to Ofcom urging it to block Rupert Murdoch’s £11.7bn bid to take over Sky, claiming it would give him too much control of UK news media and that he is not a “fit and proper” owner.
2017-04-07: The European Commission unconditionally approved 21st Century Fox's £11.7bn bid, backed by Rupert Murdoch, to take full control of Sky.
2017-04-21: The UK media regulator's investigation into Rupert Murdoch's £11.7bn takeover of Sky was delayed until after the general election, with the deadline for Ofcom's reports extended to 20 June.
2017-06-20: Labour deputy leader Tom Watson calls on the culture secretary to refer Rupert Murdoch's proposed £11.7bn takeover of Sky to competition authorities for further scrutiny.
2017-06-25: Culture secretary Karen Bradley is due to deliver her verdict this week on whether to clear 21st Century Fox's proposed £11.7bn takeover of Sky or refer it to competition authorities.
2017-06-28: Former Department of Prime Minister and Cabinet head John Menadue criticizes Rupert Murdoch and News Corp as a "disgrace" and "rogue organisation" over its push to change Australian media laws to acquire Channel Ten.
2017-07-13: Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox will not offer new concessions to culture secretary Karen Bradley to make Sky News more independent and fast-track its £11.7bn takeover of Sky.
2017-08-08: The UK government asked Ofcom for further analysis of 21st Century Fox's adherence to broadcasting standards, delaying Rupert Murdoch's proposed £11.7bn takeover of Sky.
2017-08-21: Activist group Avaaz launched the first steps of a judicial review against Ofcom over its ruling that Sky would remain "fit and proper" to hold a UK licence if acquired by Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox.
2017-09-12: The UK culture secretary referred 21st Century Fox's bid to buy the remaining 61% of Sky to the competition regulator on broadcasting standards grounds, opening a new front against Rupert Murdoch.
